title: scite: A smart citation index that displays the context of citations and classifies their intent using deep learning

extracted.subtask_description: The deployed commercial three-way classification of whether a citing sentence supports, contrasts with, or merely mentions a cited work, based on citation-context sentences alone, operating over hundreds of millions of citation statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The citing sentence's claim is backed up by the cited work; the two are in agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrasting (disputing/contradicting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The citing sentence's claim conflicts with, disputes, or contradicts findings in the cited work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The citation exists (the cited work is referenced) but the surrounding text does not take a clear evidentiary stance either way; it's a neutral/background reference rather than an explicit claim of support or contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world base-rate skew toward mentioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Average distribution across the classified corpus (25M+ full-text articles, 880M+ classified citation statements): approximately 92.6% mentioning, 6.5% supporting, 0.8% contrasting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A classifier evaluated only on raw accuracy against this distribution could score >92% by always predicting 'mentioning'; any evaluation of a support/contradiction classifier needs a metric robust to this skew (e.g., per-class recall/F1, or balanced accuracy) rather than raw accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-window-only classifiers under-detect explicit stance, over-predict mentioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent assessment of the classifier's outputs found: of 96 citations labeled 'mentioning,' reviewers judged 40 were more appropriately classified as 'supporting' and 17 more appropriately classified as 'contrasting' - over half of a sampled 'mentioning' bucket was arguably mislabeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentence/context-window-only classifiers (no full source-document verification) have a documented tendency to under-detect explicit support/contradiction and over-predict the neutral default class; treat 'mentioning' predictions from such a classifier as lower-confidence and worth secondary review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stance classification vs actual evidentiary verification (distinct targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: scite's taxonomy is about the citing author's stated intent/relationship toward the cited work, not strictly about whether the cited work's content actually substantiates the specific claim text - a subtly different target than the support/partial-support/no-support 'does this citation prove the claim is true' taxonomies used in academic quotation-accuracy audits.
